handbookNote: Florida Real Estate Broker license upgrade exam, administered by Pearson VUE under contract with the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR) / Florida Real Estate Commission (FREC) -- mechanics CONFIRMED directly from the official DBPR 'Real Estate Broker Examination Candidate Information Booklet' (effective March 2024, fetched and read directly from www2.myfloridalicense.com/servop/testing/documents/RE_broker_cib.pdf) and DBPR's own 'Real Estate Broker Requirements for licensure in the State of Florida' page (www2.myfloridalicense.com/re/documents/REBKRequirements.pdf). CONFIRMED exam structure: the broker exam is a single 100-item multiple-choice, closed-book exam with a 3.5-hour time limit, graded on a 100-point scale, requiring a score of 75 or higher to pass (materially harder than the sales associate exam's 70-point passing score) -- with no separate national/state portions (unlike Texas). The candidate booklet's own official content outline confirms 12 content areas and their exact weightings, which this bank's topic buckets are built and proportionally weighted against: Real Estate Brokerage Business 43% (licensure, brokerage entities/office requirements, ownership/management/supervision, escrow management, FREC discipline), Valuing Real Property 9%, Listing and Selling Real Property 6%, Contracts 11%, Financing 4%, Closing Transactions 12%, Federal Income Tax Laws 5%, Investment 4%, Zoning and Planning 1%, Environmental Issues 1%, Property Management 1%, and The Real Estate Market 3%. CONFIRMED education/experience prerequisites, from DBPR's own official broker requirements page: 24 months of active real estate licensure (sales associate or broker, Florida or another state) within the preceding 5 years (effective 7/1/08, Section 475.17(1)(b), F.S.); a FREC-approved 72-classroom-hour broker prelicensing course (valid 2 years); passage of this 100-question/75-point exam; completion of a FREC-approved 60-classroom-hour broker post-licensing course before the initial license expires; and 14 hours of continuing education every 2-year renewal cycle thereafter. Per the user's brief that broker content should go well beyond the sales-associate tier into escrow/trust account management, broker supervision of sales associates, and brokerage relationships, this 303-question bank concentrates its heaviest volume (85 of 303 questions, ~28%) into the Escrow Management & Trust Accounts and Brokerage Ownership/Management/Supervision buckets alone -- content grounded in F.A.C. 61J2-14.008 through .014 (escrow deposit timing: the sales associate must deliver funds to the broker by the end of the next business day, and the broker must then deposit 'immediately,' defined as by the end of the third business day; monthly written reconciliation requirements; interest-bearing escrow accounts), F.A.C. 61J2-10.032 (15-business-day notice to FREC for a good-faith-doubt or conflicting-demand escrow dispute, 30-business-day deadline to institute a settlement procedure), Section 475.25, F.S. (discipline grounds, including (1)(b) fraud/culpable negligence/breach of trust, (1)(d)1. failure to account/escrow disbursement order procedures, and (1)(k) immediate-deposit/anti-commingling; penalties up to a $5,000 fine per count, suspension up to 10 years, revocation), Sections 475.482/475.484, F.S. (Real Estate Recovery Fund, $50,000 per-claimant/transaction cap, $150,000 aggregate per-licensee cap), F.A.C. 61J2-5.016 (broker office and supervision requirements), 26 U.S.C. Section 3508 (the federal statutory-nonemployee/independent-contractor test for real estate agents), and Sections 475.700-475.719 and Part IV, F.S. (Commercial Real Estate Sales/Leasing Commission Lien Acts). Brokerage relationship content is grounded directly in Section 475.278, F.S. (transaction broker as the statutory default/presumed relationship; single agent, no brokerage relationship, and the single-agent-to-transaction-broker transition, each with their own statutorily defined duties and disclosure-timing requirements) and Section 475.2755, F.S. (designated sales associate, limited to non-residential transactions where both parties have assets of $1 million or more). The Closing Transactions bucket's math is grounded in Florida's actual documentary stamp tax and intangible tax rates (Section 201.02, F.S. -- $0.70/$100 deed doc stamps statewide, $0.60/$100 in Miami-Dade; Section 201.08, F.S. -- $0.35/$100 note doc stamps; Section 199.133, F.S. -- 0.2% nonrecurring intangible tax on new mortgages) and independently reconciled against the dollar figures in DBPR's own official sample closing problem published in the candidate booklet itself, plus the federal TRID 3-business-day Closing Disclosure delivery rule (12 C.F.R. Section 1026.19(f)). Property Management content (weighted above its nominal 1% exam share, consistent with the user's brief and this project's established broker-tier pattern) is grounded in Section 83.49, F.S. (security deposit holding/notice deadlines: 15 days to return without claim, 30 days to send a written claim notice, 15 days for the tenant to object) and Section 83.56(3)/83.67, F.S. (nonpayment notice and self-help eviction prohibition), layered on top of the same broker trust-account rules governing sales escrow. Fair Housing content is grounded in 42 U.S.C. Sections 3601-3631 (Fair Housing Act, seven protected classes, steering/blockbusting/redlining, HOPA senior-housing and Mrs. Murphy exemptions), 42 U.S.C. Sections 1981-1982 (Civil Rights Act of 1866, no exemptions), and Chapter 760, F.S. (Florida Civil Rights Act). Appraisal-theory principles (substitution, progression/regression, contribution, anticipation, highest and best use) and general contract-law concepts (void/voidable, bilateral/unilateral, executed/executory, assignment) are standard, well-corroborated real estate curriculum content rather than pinpoint statutory citations, and are flagged in-content with source_note 'hedge:general-knowledge' where appropriate, consistent with this project's grounding standard. The exact broker exam fee was not independently pinpoint-verified in this pass (a third-party source cites $36.75 for the sales associate exam, but the broker-specific fee was not separately confirmed from an official DBPR/Pearson VUE fee schedule) and is therefore omitted from this note rather than guessed. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized going rate for Real Estate tracks (applied project-wide since 2026-08-13), consistent with fl_real_estate.json, ca_re_broker.json, and tx_re_broker.json. Answer choices were drafted correct-as-choice_a throughout, then deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_fl_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all 303 questions in file order, not manual), landing at A 25.1% / B 25.1% / C 25.1% / D 24.8% -- within this project's target band.
